summary: Surge of 5xx responses across API gateway + upstream runtime crashes impacting Dedicated customers in us-east
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-12 08:40 UTC we observed a sudden increase in 5xx HTTP responses from the hosted API fronting Dedicated clusters in us-east. Error rate for affected customer BrightPages spiked from baseline ~0.2% to 12% for write/generate endpoints. Impact: customers on Dedicated capacity experienced failed completions and streaming disconnects; BrightPages reported production user-facing errors and queued retry storms. Timeline: 2026-03-12 08:40 UTC - first alert from SLO monitor; 08:42 UTC - increased 5xx in Grafana (api-gateway upstream_5xx rate); 08:47 UTC - Sentry shows repeated runtime exceptions: "kv_cache_unexpected_state" and OOM-like traces on several pods; 09:05 UTC - autoscaler attempting to add nodes but new nodes failed readiness checks. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run sustained multi-user generate workload with tokens-per-request distribution matching customer workload (long tail). 2) Observe API gateway 502/503 responses and upstream runtime restarts in the serving-runtime pods. Observed logs: - api-gateway: "upstream returned 502 Bad Gateway: connection reset" - serving-runtime (pod id rtm-us-east-7a): "panic: kv_cache inconsistent map size" and repeated GC spikes followed by restart - kube events: node pressure and kubelet readiness flapping Preliminary hypothesis: a combination of (A) a sudden increase in long-sequence requests causing heavy KV cache pressure in serving-runtime leading to inconsistent internal state and crashes, and (B) autoscaler race conditions where new nodes fail readiness due to runtime init races, amplifying overload and producing 502s at the gateway. Next steps: - Collect memory/CPU profiles and heap dumps from affected runtime pods (capture at next crash). - Gather gateway access logs correlated with pod restarts and node lifecycle events. - Run isolated reproduce on staging with similar load pattern and the same model variants. - Engage runtime on-call for a hotfix to make KV cache failure mode graceful (fall back to rebuild) and ensure readiness checks tolerate transient init conditions. - Coordinate with Customer Success to issue status update to BrightPages and recommend temporary throttle of long-sequence requests or pin to smaller model.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 09:12 UTC - Support triage: elevated 5xx confirmed; SLO monitor page 'api-upstream-5xx' firing.
2026-03-12 09:25 UTC - Observed pattern: runtime pods with highest memory allocation correspond to requests with sequence length > 2048 tokens.
2026-03-12 10:00 UTC - Autoscaler logs show several 'failed readiness' events immediately after new node provisioning; readiness probe timeout 30s.
2026-03-12 11:30 UTC - Reproduced locally in staging: sending sustained 5 RPS of long sequences causes serving-runtime process to panic within ~3 minutes under current binary v1.14.2.
2026-03-13 07:50 UTC - Runtime team hypothesizes race during KV cache rebuild; suggested mitigation: guard rebuild path and return 503 graceful retry instead of panic.
2026-03-13 09:10 UTC - Engineering created PR to add defensive checks and increase readiness probe timeout: PR #842 and api-gateway fallback PR #1203.
2026-03-14 02:30 UTC - Staging rollout of patched runtime completed; initial soak shows no panics under same load.
2026-03-14 08:00 UTC - Prepare coordinated rollout to prod us-east with canary 10% traffic and automated rollback on increased 5xx.
comments: Aisha Patel (2026-03-12 09:05): Customer BrightPages reported users seeing 'Something went wrong' on generate endpoint. Escalated to SRE and Runtime on-call. Linked Grafana alert: #alerts/4621.

Marco Chen (2026-03-12 09:40): Investigating runtime logs and kube events. Noted 'kv_cache_unexpected_state' in rtm pods. Opening runtime incident and attaching pod logs. @runtime-oncall please advise.

SRE OnCall - Leila Gomez (2026-03-12 10:10): Confirmed node readiness failures; suspect init script ttfb causing readiness probe timeouts. Increasing probe timeout as temporary mitigation. Rolling change to autoscaler config in staging.
Runtime Eng - Daniel Rossi (2026-03-13 07:00): Reproduced locally. Creating PR to guard KV rebuild path to return graceful error. Reference: github PR #842. Planning staging rollout.
Customer Success - Priya Singh (2026-03-12 10:30): Sent BrightPages interim update: engineering investigating, recommended temporary request throttling. Will update when we have ETA on fix.

Marco Chen (2026-03-14 09:20): Patch rolled to prod canary (10%). No increase in 5xx on canary over 6h. Preparing progressive rollout at 2026-03-14 12:00 UTC. Need CS copy for full resolution message.
Priya Singh (2026-03-14 09:40): Drafting customer notification: include root cause summary, workaround (throttle long sequences), and timeline for full rollout.
resolution: In progress - patch merged to runtime to avoid panic and make error mode graceful. Canary in prod holding steady; progressive rollout scheduled. Final resolution pending completion of full rollout and confirmation from BrightPages that errors stopped.
external_communications: 2026-03-12 11:00 - BrightPages interim notice: 'We are investigating an elevated error rate affecting generation requests for dedicated clusters in us-east. Our engineering team is actively triaging and we will send updates.'

2026-03-14 13:05 - BrightPages post-fix notice: 'We deployed a runtime patch to prevent upstream panics; please verify your traffic and reach out if you see residual failures. Consider temporary throttling of requests longer than 2048 tokens until next week.'
